# A failure produced in one language, and what every other language must still
# make of it.
#
# The behaviour scenarios ask whether three implementations do the same thing to
# their own stores. Nothing asked whether one can read what another WROTE, and a
# failure is where that question bites: the class is the whole retry model, it
# does not survive a process in an error object, and for as long as only one
# language wrote it down the other two silently answered "retryable" about
# refusals nobody will ever satisfy.
#
# So each language reads all of these, including the two it did not write. What
# is compared is the MEANING -- the class a reader recovers -- and never the
# sentence: three implementations word an error three ways, always will, and
# pinning wording would make every improved message a cross-language breakage.
#
# name        the file, without .json
# class       what last_failure must recover: permanent, retryable, or none
# by          what produced the record
#
# HOW THE FIRST SIX WERE MADE. Each language's own replay driver was run over
# scenarios/failure-endings.txt and the records it left in its store were taken
# as they were, with ONE edit: `spec.sources[].locator` in the three retryable
# records held the absolute path of the machine that ran them, and a corpus in a
# published repository may not carry one. The spec is not what this corpus
# tests. Every byte of `error` and of `extensions` is the language's own.
#
# legacy-no-key is not forged either: it is records/old-failed.json, written by
# the published go/v0.1.0 tag before the key existed, and it is here because
# stores hold records like it today. It carries a sentence and no class, so
# `retryable` is not a guess about it -- it is the only answer available, and it
# is the answer every reader gave before the key existed.
#
# forged-unknown-field is the one record no conforming writer can produce: the
# payload carries a field this version has never heard of. The definition
# refuses it rather than granting it ([DEF-A7]), so the reader falls back to the
# sentence and the record means what a record with no class means. That is the
# whole compatibility rule in one fixture -- an unreadable class and an absent
# class are ONE answer, and a reader that guessed at the half it understood
# would be inventing the other half.
#
# name                  class      by
go-permanent            permanent  abstraction-download/go, ErrNoFetcher
go-retryable            retryable  abstraction-download/go, ErrDigestMismatch
python-permanent        permanent  abstraction-download/python, NoSource
python-retryable        retryable  abstraction-download/python, DigestMismatch
cpp-permanent           permanent  abstraction-download/cpp, Error(permanent)
cpp-retryable           retryable  abstraction-download/cpp, Error(not permanent)
legacy-no-key           retryable  go/v0.1.0, before the key existed
forged-unknown-field    retryable  forged: a payload from a newer writer
empty-retryable retryable synthetic: valid empty diagnostic regression
empty-permanent permanent synthetic: valid empty diagnostic regression
